meta.title: One Swimmer's Comment
meta.skill_frame: Argument and evidence: one person's report standing in for a pattern.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 6.03, 6.39 and 5.88 on the three parts (107, 101 and 105 words), 6.09 together. The load is a single comment asked to stand for a daily record, so the reader has to track what one report can and cannot cover.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for argument_evidence 4.2, band 4.2, sequence 2. No external work.
source.text_status: Drafted for the band, accepted on spot check.
source.survey: A pool board note that treats one member's comment about clearer water as proof the new filter works, when the staff keep a daily test log.
source.avoided: No pool name, town, filter brand, or test result.

session.difficulty_basis: One swimmer's impression of one swim is offered as evidence about the water on every day and for every swimmer, while the pool's daily test log goes unused.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: The community pool replaced its filter in June, and the board posted a note about the change. The note says the new filter has made the water clearer for swimmers. As evidence, it quotes one member who wrote that the water felt cleaner on the first day after the change. The note repeats that comment in bold and says the board is pleased. The board paid for the work from its own fund. The note gives no reading from the pool's water tests and no count of complaints before or after the work. The filter may be an improvement, but the note points to one person's impression.
passage.part_2: Pool staff test the water every morning and record the results in a log. The note does not mention the log, and it does not print any result from it. One swimmer's comment describes one swim on one day. It cannot show what the water was like on the other days, or what other swimmers noticed. A person who expects a new filter to work may also see clearer water because they expect it. The board had a daily record within reach and chose a single comment instead. The log would show whether the water changed after the filter went in.
passage.part_3: A single comment can show that one swimmer was pleased. It cannot show that the water is clearer for everyone, or that the filter caused the change. Those claims need the test log, which covers many days and many swimmers, or a count of complaints from before and after. The note offers a feeling where a record belongs. A reader should ask for the log before accepting the board's claim about the water. The board may be right about the filter, but this note does not show it. The note would be stronger if it printed the test results for the weeks before the change.

items.prompt: The note says the new filter has done what?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. Made the water clearer for swimmers.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The note says the new filter has made the water clearer for swimmers.
tutor_only.tell: The note says the filter made the water clearer for swimmers.
help: The sentence about the filter names its effect.
It names what the water does now.
tutor_only.core_idea: Made the water clearer for swimmers.
accept_ideas: made the water clearer
cleared the water
improved the water
made the pool water clearer
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the filter made the water warmer
if_they_say.ask: The note talks about clarity. What does it say the filter made clearer?

items.prompt: What evidence does the note give for that claim?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. One member's comment that the water felt cleaner on the first day.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The note quotes one member who wrote that the water felt cleaner on the first day after the change.
tutor_only.tell: Its evidence is one member's comment about the first day after the change.
help: The sentence that begins with evidence quotes the member.
It describes one person's first day.
tutor_only.core_idea: One member's comment that the water felt cleaner on the first day.
accept_ideas: one member's comment
a swimmer said it felt cleaner
one person's first-day report
a quote from one member
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the note gives the test results
if_they_say.ask: The note mentions no test result. What single comment does it quote?

items.prompt: Why can one swimmer's comment not show that the water is clearer for everyone?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. It describes one swim on one day, not the other days or other swimmers.
tutor_only.correct_reason: One swimmer's comment describes one swim on one day and cannot show the other days or what other swimmers noticed.
tutor_only.tell: One comment covers one swim on one day, not every day or every swimmer.
help: The sentence about the one swim limits what the comment covers.
It names the days and people left out.
tutor_only.core_idea: It covers one swim on one day, not other days or other swimmers.
accept_ideas: it is only one swim on one day
it does not cover other swimmers
one person's impression is not the whole pool
it says nothing about the other days
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the member is not a good swimmer
if_they_say.ask: The issue is coverage, not skill. How many days does the comment describe?

tutor_only.full_idea: Because it covers one swim on one day, not other days or other swimmers.

items.prompt: A board member says the comment proves the filter works. What is wrong with that?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. A feeling from one swim is not a measurement, and the pool keeps a daily test log.
tutor_only.correct_reason: One person's impression is not a measurement, and the note ignores the daily test log that could show a change.
tutor_only.tell: A feeling on one day cannot prove the filter works, and the daily log was not used.
help: The sentence about expectation and the sentence about the log carry the answer.
It contrasts an impression with a daily record.
tutor_only.core_idea: One feeling is not a measurement.
accept_ideas: one feeling is not a measurement
the note ignored the test log
a comment cannot prove the filter works
expectation can change what someone notices
not_required: whether the member liked the old filter
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the member is lying
if_they_say.ask: The comment may be honest. The problem is what one comment can prove.

tutor_only.full_idea: A feeling from one swim is not a measurement, and the daily log was not used.

items.prompt: What record would show whether the filter changed the water?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The daily test log, compared before and after the change.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The pool's daily test log, which covers many days and many swimmers, compared before and after the filter went in.
tutor_only.tell: The daily test log would show the water over many days and many swimmers.
help: The sentence about the log names the record that covers many days.
It points to a record kept every morning.
tutor_only.core_idea: The daily test log, compared before and after the change.
accept_ideas: the daily water test log
the test results from before and after
the staff's morning records
the log the pool already keeps
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says a survey of swimmers would be enough
if_they_say.ask: A survey of impressions is more comments, not a measurement. What does the staff record every morning?
